ukmt-jk-2026-01.prompt: A fly has six legs and a spider has eight legs. A group of three flies and two spiders has the same number of legs in total as a group of seven chickens and some dogs. How many dogs are in the second group?

ukmt-jk-2026-02.prompt: Sritha has four copies of a straight strip of three squares in a row (a $1\times3$ rectangle). Which of the following could she not make from her four copies?

ukmt-jk-2026-03.prompt: The diagram shows a lake containing 10 islands linked with 12 bridges. What is the smallest number of bridges that would need to be closed to prevent anyone walking from island P to island Q?

ukmt-jk-2026-04.prompt: Amy and Beth are solving Maths puzzles. Beth can solve three puzzles in the time Amy can solve two. Between them they solved 30 puzzles. How many more puzzles than Amy did Beth solve?

ukmt-jk-2026-05.prompt: The mean of a set of five different positive integers is 4. What is the largest integer that could be in the set?

ukmt-jk-2026-06.prompt: A furniture store is selling sofas, love seats and chairs made from two types of identical modular pieces plus a back piece, as shown viewed from above. Including the armrests, the width of the sofa is 220 cm and the width of the love seat is 160 cm. What is the width, in cm, of the chair?

ukmt-jk-2026-07.prompt: The five keys shown fit the five padlocks. The numbers on the keys are coded by letters on the padlocks. The padlocks are DAD, BHD, AHD, ABD, HAB and the keys are 184, 812, 124, 414 and one more with a question mark. Which number is written on the remaining key?

ukmt-jk-2026-08.prompt: Pierre writes all the numbers from 1 to 20 in a row and obtains the 31-digit number 1234567891011121314151617181920. He then deletes 24 of the 31 digits so that the remaining number is as large as possible. Which number does he get?

ukmt-jk-2026-09.prompt: When Katarina added the two numbers in each row and each column of the grid $\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline a&b\\\hline c&d\\\hline\end{array}$, she obtained the results shown: row sums 2 (top) and 3 (bottom), column sums 1 (left) and 4 (right). Which of the statements below is true?

ukmt-jk-2026-10.prompt: Kush spent five days walking in the mountains. He started on Monday and his last day was Friday. Each day he walked 2 km more than he had done the day before. The total distance he walked was 70 km. What distance did Kush walk on Thursday?

ukmt-jk-2026-11.prompt: On Iyla's island there are some lions, some tigers and some jaguars. Two-thirds of the animals are not lions; three-quarters of the animals are not tigers; 84 of the animals are not jaguars. How many animals are on Iyla's island?

ukmt-jk-2026-12.prompt: How many positive integers between 10 and 2026 have all their digits the same and are divisible by 3?

ukmt-jk-2026-13.prompt: Beads numbered 1 to $n$, where $n>1$, are threaded onto a bracelet. What is the smallest value of $n$ for which this can be done in such a way that no two consecutive numbers are next to each other?

ukmt-jk-2026-14.prompt: Five children each writes down a different positive integer. One writes down a square, one writes down a cube, one writes down a prime, one writes down an odd integer and one writes down an even integer. What is the smallest possible total of the five integers?

ukmt-jk-2026-15.prompt: In an orchard, 80% of the trees were apple trees and the rest were pear trees. Last summer, the apple weevil killed some of the apple trees but no pear trees. Now 50% of the trees are apple trees. What percentage of the apple trees were killed by the apple weevil?

ukmt-jk-2026-16.prompt: The integers 1 to 20 are written on a board. Patricia erases three of the integers and replaces them with their sum. She repeats this process until only two integers remain. What is the sum of these two remaining integers?

ukmt-jk-2026-17.prompt: Four players each scored goals in a handball match. Each of them scored a different number of goals. Of the four, Will scored the fewest goals. The other three scored twenty goals in total. What is the largest number of goals Will could have scored?

ukmt-jk-2026-18.prompt: Rafael uses three squares to create a shape. The first has side-length 3 cm. The second has side-length 5 cm and one of its vertices is placed in the centre of the first square. The third square has side-length 7 cm and one of its vertices is placed in the centre of the second square, as shown in the diagram. The top edges of all three squares are parallel. What is the total shaded area in $\text{cm}^2$?

ukmt-jk-2026-19.prompt: Nell wants to write the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 in the five cells in the diagram (a row of three cells with two further cells below the first) so that any number directly below another number is greater than that number and any number directly to the right of another number is greater than that number. In how many ways can she do this?

ukmt-jk-2026-20.prompt: Ali said Dele ate the cake. Dele said Billi ate the cake. Billi said Callie ate the cake. Callie said she didn't eat the cake and Eddie said that he did. I know Ali didn't eat the cake, that one of the others did and that only one of them is telling the truth. Who ate the cake?

ukmt-jk-2026-21.prompt: Eight kangaroos stood in a line, as shown. At some point, two kangaroos standing next to each other and facing each other exchanged places. This was repeated until no further exchanges were possible. How many exchanges were made?

ukmt-jk-2026-22.prompt: A bag contains only red marbles and green marbles. For every five marbles that are chosen, at least one will be red. For every six marbles that are chosen, at least one will be green. What is the largest number of marbles the bag can contain?

ukmt-jk-2026-23.prompt: Freda likes even numbers, Greta likes numbers divisible by 3 and Hattie likes numbers divisible by 5. A basket contains eight balls, each with a number written on. The three girls went in turn to the basket and took all the balls with a number on that they like. Freda collected balls with numbers 32 and 52 on, Greta collected balls with numbers 24, 33 and 45 on and Hattie collected balls with numbers 20, 25 and 35 on. In what order did the girls go to the basket?

ukmt-jk-2026-24.prompt: Jacques wants to write a positive integer in each box in the diagram (a pyramid of 1, 2, 3 and 4 boxes in rows) so that each integer above the bottom row is the sum of the two integers immediately below it. What is the largest number of odd integers that Jacques can write?

ukmt-jk-2026-25.prompt: Julia has four different coloured pencils and wants to use some or all of them to colour the map of four regions shown in the diagram. She wants to ensure that two regions that share a common border are shaded in different colours. In how many different ways can she colour the map?
